messages:
jin: FYI I'm seeing a ~15% p95 regression on long-context decode after the selector change this morning. Profiling attached in thread.
chris: ugh. is that for prefills or decode path only?
maria: can you paste the perf snapshot / top callers?
jin: mostly decode. shortctx looks fine. here's the top of the CPU timeline:
```
decode_loop -> kernel_dispatch (30%) -> memcpy (18%) -> kv_cache_lookup (12%) -> kernel_launch_overhead (10%)
```
devon: kernel_launch_overhead is suspicious. did the selector start splitting kernels more aggressively?
jin: yes — new architecture-aware picks swapped in a different fused kernel for medium seqs. on A100 it increases dispatch overhead for long runs.
chris: which kernel lib? cuBLAS or our fused CUDA kernels?
jin: fused CUDA kernels (v4) + a different layout that triggers small per-step kernels. cuBLAS 12.1 changes made the matmul path faster per-call but launch cost kills long sequences.
maria: could be batching too small as well. are we autoscaling batch window differently per path?
jin: batching heuristics unchanged. it's the path flip frequency: sequences near the length threshold are flipping between prefill and decode kernels every few tokens -> repeated kernel handoffs + KV touch.
devon: flipping sounds bad. we should add a safety guard so path doesn't change for an active sequence unless it crosses a bigger margin. basically a debounce on path selection.
chris: agreed. propose: sticky path for N tokens once chosen, and only allow re-eval after M tokens or on significant seq growth. numbers?
maria: start with sticky=32 tokens, re-eval interval=64. also pin KV cache layout during sticky window to avoid reallocation.
jin: tried sticky=16 during perf test. p95 dropped back to baseline, median slightly up. will run 32 next.
infra-bot: perf-bench: started job perf/seqlen/1976543210/1. ETA ~20m.
jin: quick microbench I ran: toggling selector to prefer larger fused kernel reduced calls but increased per-call latency; overall decode cost up on longctx. attaching sample timeline snippet:
```
[ timeline ]
0ms - prefill done
10ms - decode tokens 1..40 -> kernelA launch x40 (high overhead)
420ms - decode tokens 41..200 -> kernelB fused x160 (lower overhead per call)
```
chris: so the cost amortization is wrong for long runs. path gating should consider expected remaining tokens. we need an estimate of remaining length at path decision time.
maria: we have token_count_remaining heuristic from router. use that to bias kernel picks: prefer lower-launch-overhead kernel if remaining > threshold.
devon: also link to KV cache behavior: when we flip kernel we change KV layout and sometimes evict cached KV pages -> causes memcpy spikes. pinning KV during sticky window avoids that.
jin: test notes: with sticky=32 + KV pin, p95 back within 2% of before-change. throughput neutral.
chris: good. plan: 1) ship a short-lived safety guard (sticky=32, KV pin) behind feature flag, 2) instrument path flip rate metric, 3) run canary on 10% dedicated nodes.
maria: add a metric: path_switches_per_request and kv_evictions_during_request. alert if > 0.1 switches/request.
devon: also add a unit microbench that simulates borderline seqs to prevent regressions during autotune.
jin: I'll open a PR with the flag and tests. will include perf results and flame graphs.
chris: thanks. if infra-bot can roll the canary once PR is merged that'd be ideal.
infra-bot: canary pipeline queued: canary/deploy/1976543210. notify channel on completion. :rocket:
maria: nice work catching this. small tweak, big impact.
jin: yep. will post PR link shortly.
